summary: Adds next GIF frame as an ARGB pixel array, top row first (0xAARRGGBB).
description: Adds next GIF frame as an ARGB pixel array, top row first (0xAARRGGBB). The alpha channel is ignored. The frame is not written immediately, but is actually deferred until the next frame is received so that timing data can be inserted. Invoking finish() flushes all frames. The size of the first frame is used for all subsequent frames; frames of another size are scaled with nearest-neighbour sampling.

summary: "abs" is an abbreviation for "absolute value.
description: "abs" is an abbreviation for "absolute value." The absolute value of a number is its distance from 0. A simpler way to describe an absolute value is that it makes any number positive. If it is negative, it becomes positive, and if it is positive, it stays the same.

summary: "asin" is the abbreviation for "arcsine" and is also sometimes written as sin−1.

summary: "atan" is the abbreviation for "arctangent" and is also sometimes written as tan−1.
description: "atan" is the abbreviation for "arctangent" and is also sometimes written as tan−1. When given the ratio (in decimal form) of the length of the opposite side and adjacent side of a right triangle, it finds the angle.

summary: This always rounds the number up to the least whole number greater than or equal to the number.

summary: "cos" is the abbreviation for "cosine.
description: "cos" is the abbreviation for "cosine." The cosine of an angle is the ratio between the length of the side adjacent (next to) it on the triangle and the length of the hypotenuse. In the picture above, the cosine of angle A is equal to side "adjacent" divided by side "hypotenuse".

summary: "e" is an abbreviation for "Euler's number", which is about 2.
description: "e" is an abbreviation for "Euler's number", which is about 2.718. With the e^ function, e is multiplied by itself the value number of times. For example, if the value is 3, the answer would be e3, or e×e×e, which is about 20.086.
returns: e to the power of that value

summary:
This always rounds the number down to the greatest whole number less than or equal to the
number.
description: This always rounds the number down to the greatest whole number less than or equal to the number. For example, floor(1.73) = 1 and floor(-2.74) = -3.

summary: Calculates a number between two numbers at a specific increment.
description: Calculates a number between two numbers at a specific increment. The amt parameter is the amount to interpolate between the two values where 0.0 equal to the first point, 0.1 is very near the first point, 0.5 is half-way in between, etc. The lerp function is convenient for creating motion along a straight path and for drawing dotted lines.

summary: ln is "natural log.
description: ln is "natural log." It figures out how many times e would have to be multiplied by itself to get the value. For example, if the value was 148.4, the answer would be about 5 because e5 (e×e×e×e×e) is around 148.4.

summary: "Log" is short for "logarithm.
description: "Log" is short for "logarithm." The log function figures out how many times 10 must be multiplied by itself to get the value. For example, if the value is 100, the answer is 2 because 10×10 is 100.
returns: the log to base 10 of that value

summary: Re-maps a number from one range to another.

In the first example above, the number 25 is converted from a value in the range of 0 to 100 into a value that ranges from the left edge of the window (0) to the right edge (width).

As shown in the second example, numbers outside the range are not clamped to the minimum and maximum parameters values, because out-of-range values are often intentional and useful.

summary: "mod" is an abbreviation for "modulo".
description:
"mod" is an abbreviation for "modulo". Modulo returns what is left over when the first input is divided by the second.

The answer takes the sign of the second input, as the Scratch block does, so mod(-7, 3) is 2 rather than the -1 Java's own % would give. That is what makes it useful for wrapping a value into a range: a sprite whose x has gone negative still lands somewhere sensible.
returns: what is left of the first value after dividing by the second

returns: what is left of the first value after dividing by the second

summary: "sin" is an abbreviation for "sine.
description: "sin" is an abbreviation for "sine." The sine of an angle is the ratio between the length of the side that is opposite (across) the triangle from it and the length of the hypotenuse (the side that is across from the right angle). In the picture above, the sine of angle A is equal to side "opposite" divided by side "hypotenuse".

summary: "sqrt" is an abbreviation for "square root.
description: "sqrt" is an abbreviation for "square root." A number that is squared is multiplied by itself. For example, when 2 is squared, the answer is 2×2, which is 4. When a number is square rooted, the answer is the number that was squared to get it. So, the square root of 4 is 2. Similarly, the square root of 2 is about 1.414213562373095 because 1.4142135623730952 (1.414213562373095 × 1.414213562373095) is close to 2.
returns: the square root of the value

summary: "tan" is the abbreviation for "tangent.
description: "tan" is the abbreviation for "tangent." The tangent of an angle is the ratio between the length of the side adjacent to it and the side opposite of it. In the picture above, the tangent of angle A is equal to side "opposite" divided by side "adjacent".

summary: The 10^ function multiplies 10 times itself the value number of times.
